line_text: What? After all that, you've had it the whole time? So then it's your fault that thing showed up! / You...you're the one who bought it! / You blame me for everything! / Well I never! / I've heard quite enough out of the two of you. The Rain Lord is held fast inside the urn. It shouldn't trouble us again any time soon.

trigger: requested by イベント管理.ギルガメクリア_再生
line_text: Which brings us to you. You've done us a great service. You deserve to know the whole story. You see, the magicks of the urn had grown weak, so it became necessary to replenish its stores. The Rain Lord within has the power to quiet the beasts of the plains, and in turn, the power to keep us safe. But the urn's power fades with time. When a new Rain Lord appears, we must seal it within the urn to keep our plains safe. / Then, that means... / All this didn't have anything to do with the tortoiseshell I bought? So how come you told us never to buy tortoiseshell? / I never said anything of the sort. I said no matter the price it might fetch at market, you should not kill a tortoise simply to harvest its shell. This is true of all things, not merely tortoises. Whether hunting beasts or gathering herbs, take only what you need, no more. / & Yes ma'am. / Now, I'll be taking the urn back. Nanau, Roaklo. You've served the village well. As have you, young man. Thank you.

speaker: Elder Brunoa
line_text: It can get quite hot here in Giza, but it's not all that bad if you can find a nice spot in the shade. Take care before heading out to the plains. Our children don't leave without making the proper preparations. Neither should you. / Don't go out to the plains unprepared. Speak with Arjie before you go if there's anything you need. / Giza Plains has two seasons, the Dry and the Rains. I don't smell rain on the air...I'd say the Dry ought last a while longer. You look like you're getting swept up in something big, boy. See it doesn't sweep you away, eh? / If you find yourself in Giza during the Rains, be careful. The Rains see much fiercer beasts than the Dry. / They tell me the fallen tree blocking the road to Kerwon was washed away by the Rains. The way south through Starfall Field is open. If you're heading that way, see you're well provisioned before setting out. Changes in the land mean changes in the beasts that walk them. / I was walking through the plains several days past when I was overcome by the feeling some great power had been lost. I pray it is no ill omen. / Whatever comes to the world beyond the plains, Giza will always be Giza. The sun, the earth, the winds...if we have these, we have our home. / If you ever need a place to rest, you are always welcome in our village.

speaker: Elder Brunoa
line_text: You've a troubled look, child. What's the matter? Ah, come from Rabanastre seeking a sunstone, have you? As you might have guessed from the name, sunstones contain the power of the sun. You'll often find them used as a source of heat or light. Here we leave all things sunstone to Masyua. You should be able to find her near the dark crystal. / Do you see the large black stone behind my tent? That is a dark crystal. You'll not find them outside Giza Plain. The dark surfaces of the crystal drink in the light of the sun. / You need a sunstone, yes? Best speak with Masyua about that. She should be just behind my tent.

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, イベント管理.太陽石できた後半_再生
speaker: Elder Brunoa
line_text: I'm glad to see you were able to find a sunstone for yourself. Heading back to Rabanastre soon, then? Come visit us whenever you like. We will be here until the coming of the Rains.

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, イベント管理.ギルガメクリア_再生
speaker: Elder Brunoa
line_text: That ring... But...where? Where did you find it? / That's the very ring. The ring he gave me on our wedding day... But I was careless, and I lost it. So precious a thing, yet I lost it! Sadeen saw how sad I was, so he set off into the plains to find it. He knew the Rains would soon come, but still he went. I waited and waited. Then the Rains came, and I could wait no more. He never returned. Even after all these years, I could never bring myself to leave this place. / I'd given up on ever finding that ring. But I never stopped thinking about it. And here out of the blue you bring it to me! Thank you. Thank you so much. / I believe you really did meet him. I do. And in time, I know I will meet him again too. I could ask for no more. Thank you.

trigger: requested by 常駐監督.init, イベント管理.ギルガメクリア_再生
speaker: Elder Brunoa
line_text: The Rain Lord, the slaying of the tortoises, the Rains on Giza... Are they related? I do not know. But it is important that the children learn the lesson of moderation. If this parable helps them learn—and I think it has—that is enough. / You will find many tortoises in Giza during the Rains. There are those who even call southwest Giza the "Land of the Tortoise."

Well, hello! The wary traveler never passes the chance to restock his supplies. / The children still work, even in this heat. I guess I should try to follow their example. / We will leave before the Rains come. If there's anything you want to buy, now's the time. / I used to live in Rabanastre, before I met my husband. Then I moved here. I only get to see him during the Rains, but I'm happy all the same. / The skies are clear, the food and drink fresh and delicious. The people are good, hard working folk. I've never regretted coming to Giza.
Well, hello! The wary traveler never passes the chance to restock his supplies. / A ring? I have the ring my husband gave me. I don't think I'll be accepting another. Sorry!

speaker: Lesina
line_text: The men are off on their business, while we women mind the village. Even the children do their part. They make their mistakes, of course, but they learn from them! / Have you heard? They're saying the Princess is alive! And I'd thought she committed suicide... I'm not sure what to believe anymore. Those people in the city like nothing more than to gossip, don't they. / Have you been to the garif village? Our elder and their chieftain go way back, but they haven't seen each other in a cockatrice's age. I make trips to their village to trade sunstones for medicinal herbs, hides...you name it. And the kids just love that nanna cheese they make. / Things in Rabanastre finally start to settle down, and now I hear a new storm's brewin'? You take care of yourself, okay? Remember, where there's life, there's hope.

speaker: Lesina
line_text: You want to give me a ring? That's sweet, but you shouldn't joke about such things.

speaker: Lesina
line_text: Is that an errmonea leaf you have there? Ah, a gift from old Sugumu, is it? How considerate! Normally have to head all the way down to Ozmone Plain for this, but the road south hasn't been clear lately. / Thank you for bringing this to me. Here's a little something for your trouble. / How's Sugumu been? They mostly send younger folks these days, so I haven't seen him in a while. Say hello for me, if you get the chance. / Errmonea leaf isn't easy to come by. Sometimes I have to send all the way to the southern reaches of Ozmone Plain for it. They may be on the reclusive side, and I still don't know what to make of those masks, but I've never met a garif I didn't like.

speaker: Dania
line_text: Don't worry, they won't bite! These cockatrices are tame as can be. Aren't they just the fluffiest, cutest things you've ever seen? / This breed of cockatrice does real well in dry climates, so they're perfect for Giza. Proud and strong...beautiful creatures, don't you think? / If you plan on touching one, say something so they know you're comin' first. And you wanna be real gentle. Gets to be you know what they're thinkin'. Cockatrices are such quiet, calm creatures, sometimes I think they may even be intelligent. / Every now and then, I could swear the cockatrices understand what I'm saying. I'm probably just lettin' my imagination get the better of me.

speaker: Dania
line_text: Wonderful! I had thought you'd say yes. Now, let me tell you just what's going on. A vile creature called a cluckatrice has made its nest in the land to the east. Recently, its eggs hatched, and now it's viler than ever. What's worse, the cluckatrice shies away when people approach. It's clever, this one. For our sake, and the sake of the cockatrices, kill the cluckatrice and every one of its foul brood! / I spied the cluckatrice on the Gizas North Bank. It's not much of a bank during the Dry, but you'll find it to the southeast of the village. The cluckatrice's nest must be near there, but I have no idea how to go about drawing it out of hiding. Try as I might, I haven't come up with anything. Perhaps you should ask the children? They're often out on the plains. Maybe they can help. / What!? You won't go on the hunt? Why...you're not in it for the cockatrices at all, are you! / The cluckatrice that's nested in the plains is nothing but trouble for us. The poor cockatrices are scared out of their feathers. I saw the cluckatrice and its brood on the Gizas North Bank, to the southeast of the village. Its nest must be nearby! But it shies away when people approach. There must be a way to draw it out, but I haven't a clue. Speak with the children, if you haven't already. / You did it! You got rid of the cluckatrice and its chicks! Here's your bounty, as agreed. Thank you so much! / I can finally walk the cockatrices again. You wouldn't know it to look at them, but they scare very easily. / The chicks may have been cute, but make no mistake, we're better off with that cluckatrice gone. What? Like our cockatrices? Don't be silly, they couldn't look more different!

speaker: Dania
line_text: Would you look at this... All our cockatrices, gone! I'd always left the pen open, and they never tried to escape before. What do you think got into them? There's nothin' to do but head out lookin' for 'em, but I don't even know where to start. I can't blame Terra for this... It's my fault. She wasn't ready for the responsibility. / I'd always left the pen open, and they never tried to escape before. What do you think got into them? Considering how tame our cockatrices are, I wouldn't be surprised to find them in cities, villages...anywhere with people. / I figured they'd be somewhere with lots of people. I'm still worried for the ones that haven't come back yet, though. Poor Terra's been miserable, but she shouldn't blame herself. If she keeps looking after them, sooner or later she'll come to understand them. / I wasn't sure what we were going to do, but they're all back safe and sound now. In fact, they seem better than ever. Like they actually learned a thing or two on their travels. Of course, Terra's thrilled they're back, too.

speaker: Dania
line_text: That ring looks quite old. If you really want to impress, you should find something newer, something fashionable.

speaker: Masyua
line_text: Have you come to see the dark crystals? Not everyone takes well to the heat of the Giza Plains. We don't have much to offer, but you're welcome to rest here, if you like. These dark crystals absorb the light of the sun, until they shine with a brilliant light. People are always surprised just how bright they shine. / The quality's a bit poor... I won't be able to give you a very good price. / Acceptable quality, I suppose. Pretty average, truth be told. / A nice stone, this one. I'll give you a good price. / This is a sunstone of the highest grade! You don't see many of these. / Should you change your mind, do let me know. / Jinn and my son have been getting along just fine. A little friendly competition can be a healthy thing, really. / Take the shadestone I gave you to the shining crystals on the plains. When the energy gauge is full, the sunstone is ready. If you have trouble finding the crystals, stop and take a look around. Remember, I pay well for stones of quality. / There, now you've the shadestone you need. Fill it with the light of the dark crystals and return when you've made a sunstone. I pay well for stones of high grade! / I pay well for stones of high grade. I wish you you luck! / You're always welcome, if you change your mind. We pay well for stones of a high grade, should you need a few extra gil. / The garif live to the south, in northern Kerwon. They are an ancient race, who live by the ways of their ancestors. They wear masks from the day they're born until the day they die. / Elder Brunoa leads our people, watching over us, giving us advice. I pray she is with us for many years to come.

speaker: Terra
line_text: I know what that ring's for! You give that to somebody you want to marry!

speaker: Shurry; Cockatrice
line_text: (It looks like it has an itch on its back.) / (It looks a little down in the beak.) / (There's a glint of wisdom in its eyes.) / Ever 'eard of a nanna? It's this green beast wot they breed inna southlands. I 'eard there ain't 'ardly a bit of 'em they don't use fer summink! Lookin' at 'em, I can't 'ardly tell whether they're birds or beasts. But any'ow, they ain't nowhere near as good-lookin' as us cockatrices. / I'm bloomin' ex'austed, I am! Can't get a moment's kip wiv them lot carryin' on! / Them sweets wot that garif bloke gave me fer bring back 'ere smelled so good, I 'ad 'em on the way. Ooooh, an' they was summink else, darlin'! Gorgeous don't do 'em justice, I can tell ya! / Accordin' to them Garifs, Brunoa an' that chief o' theirs 'ave got a lotta wot you might call 'ist'ry. Eh? Not relations! I di'n't mean it like that! Wot I meant fer say was that 'e feels this, like, big...debt o' gra'itude to 'er. Dunno why, though!

speaker: Moomer; Cockatrice
line_text: (It looks like it wants to be left alone.) / (It looks a little down in the beak.) / (There's a glint of wisdom in its eyes.) / No blokes 'round 'ere, wot wiv 'em all 'avin' gone off diggin' for shadestones. Where? I ain't tellin' ya! The dough wot they make off the sunstones puts nosh in me gob, see? / That bloomin' cluckatrice can cluck right off! Who does she think she is, eh!? Struttin' about like she owns the place...an' 'elpin' 'erself to our feed!? It's a bleedin' OUTRAGE! Bleedin' stupid bloomin' bird... / If I'd've known they'd be strappin' such 'eavy loads on me back, I'd've made out like I was a bloomin' cockatrice! Cor...it ain't 'alf 'ard bein' a chocobo. / Got meself in a right mess over in Balfon'eim. These nutters got it inta their 'eads I was a cockatrice! A bloomin' cockatrice, mind you! They stuffs me in this crate, an' I'm in a ship 'fore I knew wot'd 'it me! Luckily, I still 'ad me wits about me, 'an it weren't long 'fore I gave 'em the slip. Couldn't walk straight fer days, though. Bleedin' ruffians.

speaker: Sassan; Cockatrice
line_text: (It looks like it wants to tell you something. Then again, maybe not.) / (It looks a little down in the beak.) / (There's a glint of wisdom in its eyes.) / 'Ave you 'eard the latest? Apparently, Tott fancies Camina. But the thing is, right, Camina fancies Jinn! Heh! 'Umes, eh? Wot're they like? Any'ow, it looks like Tott an' Jinn've got more to sort out than just who makes the best sunstones, if ya know wot I mean! / So the chick's back now, an' it's nuffin but cheep cheep cheep, mornin', night 'n' day! It's doin' me 'ead in! / 'Ave yer 'eard? Torrie said as she'd marry me! We'll make the 'appiest couple in the 'ist'ry o' the plains! / I ain't 'eard a bleedin' word outta Torrie. I'm itchin' to get on wiv the cerem'ny, but I'm startin' to think she might've 'ad second thoughts! I bloomin' knew I shoulda brought 'er back wiv me when I 'ad the chance.

speaker: Chit; Cockatrice
line_text: (It stares at you with beady eyes...) / (It looks a little down in the beak.) / (There's a glint of wisdom in its eyes.) / Dania's a diamond of an 'erdswoman, ya know. She don't 'ave to look at us twice to know if we've got our feathers in a knot. An' 'er massages're summink else! I can 'ardly keep from noddin' off when she does me neck. Eh? Wot neck!? Summink up wiv yer eyes, is there!? / Me bloomin' feathers've started fallin' out! That's me nerves, that is! If summink ain't done soon, I'm gonna be naked as the day I 'atched! / When I come back, little Terra was cryin' 'er eyes out, poor love. I di'n't realize we'd given 'er such a fright. Won't be lettin' that 'appen again. / Yer know them vieras? Well, the older they get, the longer their ears get. Don't believe me? Jus' look at Jote, Fran, an' Mjrn. There's yer proof! Well, that's wot I reckon, anyway.

speaker: Nanau
line_text: I knew it! I had a feeling about you. Well, let's get on with it then. What do you say? I'm sure you know that we live here only during the Dry, and leave the village come the Rains. There are, however...circumstances preventing us from leaving now. / I keep tellin' you, I didn't know the hairpin was made of tortoiseshell! And I don't remember you complainin' when I gave it to you. "Oh, it's beeaauutiful!" Hmph. / Quiet! If I hadn't sent you to Rabanastre to sell our sunstones we wouldn't be in this trouble in the first place. You only brought me the hairpin hoping it would keep me from noticin' how much money you had spent. You meant to trick me! And to add insult to your deception, you find me a hairpin of tortoiseshell. What has Elder Brunoa said about tortoiseshell? You're incorrigible! / (sigh) I'm sorry you had to see that. Please, allow me to continue. A great beast known as the gil snapper once ruled these plains. Our people call it the Rain Lord. A fearsome tortoise, it fights as a beast possessed in battle. Our forefathers drove it away...but now it has returned. No doubt this hairpin my brother brought me has wakened the curse and stirred its wrath. / & What!? / Oh...oh, really? Are you sure? Well, I suppose you would know, wouldn't you. My apologies. / I can see why you'd hesitate to hunt such a creature. The gil snapper is protected by a hard, thick shell...it will be no easy kill. But think on its name... Surely it's not called a gil snapper for nothing. What of the riches you might be passing by!? / I hear the conviction of your words. Take the urn my brother is carrying. Brunoa prepared the urn to seal away the evil of the Rain Lord. You must point the urn at the creature as you land the killing blow. / The Rain Lord, this gil snapper, is to the east, in a place called the Tracks of the Beast. Heavy rains draw it out to wreak its havoc. Unfortunately we are unfamiliar with Giza during the Rains. The wadis overflow with water, paths wash away...I don't know how to reach it. Still, there must be some way! Please, search Giza and put an end to our curse! / I've heard the gil snapper is true to its name. A fortune fit for the Lord of Giza awaits the person who can kill it! Beware... I've heard its shell is hard enough to deflect even the finest blades!
